name: Goldenes Dachl
kurzbeschreibung: The Golden Roof in Innsbruck's historic old town is Tyrol's golden landmark: 2,657 fire-gilded copper tiles, sculpted reliefs, and Emperor Maximilian's museum.
beschreibung:
Overview

The world-famous Golden Roof (Goldenes Dachl) on Herzog-Friedrich-Straße in the historic pedestrian heart of Innsbruck is the defining landmark of the Tyrolean capital and one of Austria's premier late-Gothic architectural monuments. Shimmering with 2,657 fire-gilded copper shingles, this ornate royal oriel balcony has reigned over the vibrant central city square for more than five centuries. Regarded as a consummate masterpiece of transitional late-Gothic and early-Renaissance design, the landmark magnetically draws visitors from across all continents. It symbolizes the golden era of Innsbruck around the year 1500, when the city under Emperor Maximilian I rose to become the vibrant political and cultural nexus of a worldwide empire.

Route & Requirements

The ceremonial bay was commissioned between 1497 and 1500 on the grand facade of the Neuhof palace, the former sovereign residence of the Tyrolean counts. The occasion celebrated the dawn of the new century alongside Maximilian's marriage to Bianca Maria Sforza of Milan. Court master builder Nikolaus Türing the Elder oversaw construction, while court painter Jörg Kölderer crafted the vibrant frescoes. The roof is crowned by exactly 2,657 fire-gilded copper shingles that gleam like solid gold in the alpine sunlight. Intricately carved sandstone reliefs depict Maximilian surrounded by his wives, court jesters, imperial coats of arms, and the famous Moorish dancers performing acrobatic contortions. The royal balcony functioned as an imperial box for observing tournaments and bustling market life below. Today, the building houses the Golden Roof Museum, featuring interactive displays, authentic artifacts, and a dedicated children's trail exploring the Emperor's life.

Visit & Arrival

The exterior view in the pedestrian zone can be admired free of charge around the clock year-round. The Golden Roof Museum operates May to September daily 10:00 to 17:00; October to April Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 17:00 (closed Mondays). Admission: adults €6.00, concessions €3.50, youth under 19 free. Admission is free with the Innsbruck Card. Reaching the site: from Innsbruck Central Station, stroll 10 minutes along the pedestrian boulevards into the old town; trams stop at Marktplatz or Maria-Theresien-Straße. Motorists can park in the Altstadtgarage at Innrain.

Tips

The pedestrian plaza before the monument is paved with level flagstones and fully accessible. The museum itself is equipped with an elevator, offering step-free access for wheelchair users. The best photographic perspective on the gleaming gilded tiles is in the bright morning sunlight or from the viewing gallery of the historic City Tower (Stadtturm) directly opposite. An evening visit is equally enchanting when dramatic illumination bathes the gilded roof in a warm, majestic glow.
